cards.headline: Navigation app for visually impaired people expanded to 15 new transport locations
bullets: A navigation app for blind people now works at 15 more transport spots.
The app uses audio guides to help people find their way underground and indoors.
It works without internet and learns how each person walks to get more accurate.
New locations include busy stations like Yishun, Marina Bay, Dhoby Ghaut, and Outram Park.

cards.headline: I thought it was red watercolour. It was blood: Dad of girl, 9, who was run over by taxi in 2024
bullets: A taxi hit a nine-year-old girl crossing the road in February 2024.
The girl's father mistook her blood for red watercolour paint.
She suffered multiple injuries and was hospitalised for three days.
The taxi driver was fined $500 and given nine demerit points.
The father is urging drivers to be more careful on the roads.

cards.headline: Identity thief forged NRIC and tried to get $2.9m loan using victim’s landed property as collateral
bullets: Someone tried to get a $2.9 million loan using a fake NRIC and a victim's house as collateral.
The scammer used a forged NRIC and other documents to try and borrow money.
The victim discovered the fraud when he received a letter about a legal document lodged against his property.
Another person was also targeted in a similar scam, almost losing over $2 million.
Police and government agencies are investigating the impersonation cases.

cards.headline: Gel-based cooling wear trialled in Singapore can potentially reduce body heat by 9 deg C
bullets: New clothes with special gel beads can lower skin temperature by up to 9 deg C.
The gel absorbs body heat and slowly releases it through water evaporation.
The cooling wear needs no batteries and can be reused after washing.
It is being tested at worksites like NS Square and by PSA Singapore.
The company hopes to lower costs if more companies adopt the cooling clothes.

cards.headline: TCM practitioners can join hands with eligible clinics to manage patients’ health: Koh Poh Koon
bullets: TCM clinics and practitioners can propose joint patient care plans from next week.
This allows TCM to work with Healthier SG clinics for better health outcomes.
Accredited TCM clinics and those onboarded for over a year can join.
The government wants TCM providers to help with preventive care advice.
More details on a new TCM practitioner accreditation framework will be shared in July.

cards.headline: 'Find a moment for yourself': Why Singaporean artist Amanda Heng is inviting people to just rest in Venice
bullets: Singaporean artist Amanda Heng created an art installation called 'A Pause' at the Venice Biennale.
The installation invites visitors to slow down and find a moment to rest.
Heng's work is inspired by the idea of rest and her own ageing body.
Visitors can sit, lean, or lie down in the space to relax.
The art piece uses shallow wooden steps and large windows to encourage stillness.

cards.headline: Grab extends fuel surcharge, higher GrabCab metered fare rate until end July amid fuel price volatility
bullets: Grab is keeping the S$0.90 fuel surcharge and higher GrabCab fares until July 31.
The surcharge applies to all rides except standard and metered taxis.
Grab says all extra charges go directly to drivers, not the company.
GrabCab metered fares will stay at S$0.27 per 400m for the first 10km.

cards.headline: Guardiola to end decade-long Man City reign at end of season
bullets: Pep Guardiola is leaving Manchester City at the end of the season after 10 years.
He has won six Premier League titles, including four in a row.
Guardiola also won three FA Cups, five League Cups, and the Champions League.
His final game in charge will be against Aston Villa on Sunday.

cards.headline: US mortgage rates hit highest since August as war fans inflation
bullets: US mortgage rates hit 6.51%, the highest since August.
This is the biggest weekly jump in mortgage rates since late March.
War is pushing up oil prices, inflation, and bond yields.
Despite higher rates, US home sales and new listings are surprisingly strong.
Buyers are paying less than the 6.86% rate seen last year.

cards.headline: European champions Spain on quest to regain World Cup crown
bullets: Spain are favourites to win the World Cup after winning Euro 2024.
France, who lost the last final, aim to win the World Cup again.
Norway returns to the World Cup with star striker Erling Haaland.
Iran has a chance to face the US if they advance from the group stage.
Egypt's star player Mohamed Salah will leave Liverpool this season.

cards.headline: China’s housing slump shows signs of bottoming out. We’ve been here before
bullets: China's housing prices in top cities rose slightly from February to April.
This follows a 38% drop in prices since 2021.
About 90 million apartments in China are empty or unfinished.
Many Chinese families lost significant savings as property values fell.
Some analysts believe the market is stabilising, others are not so sure.

cards.headline: Ban on land sales, new launches for developers that deliver ‘defect-ridden’ projects
bullets: Developers with bad projects may be banned from selling new homes for up to five years.
New rules stop developers with major defects or safety issues from bidding on land sales.
Authorities can suspend sales of new projects by 'errant' developers for up to five years.
Homebuyers will be able to see which developers are penalized for shoddy work.

cards.headline: S'pore pet groomer, 45, has S$2,000 scissors confiscated after Scoot counter staff wrongly tells her to put them in carry-on
bullets: A pet groomer lost over S$2,000 worth of scissors after Scoot staff gave wrong advice.
She was told to put scissors in carry-on, but security said they must be checked.
The airline has apologised to the woman for the mistake.
She had to throw away seven pairs of scissors before her flight.

cards.headline: 'No breathing, no pulse': S'porean doctor, 29, responds to collapsed Virgin Active gymgoer, helps restore heartbeat before ambulance arrives
bullets: A doctor at Virgin Active Marina One helped a man who collapsed with no pulse or breathing.
The doctor, Tan Tuan Hao, 29, started CPR immediately after assessing the situation.
Gym staff brought an AED, and another gymgoer helped with CPR while the doctor used the AED.
The AED shock helped the man regain consciousness before the ambulance arrived.

cards.headline: Boy, 9, allegedly filmed in toilet cubicle at Jurong Point, police investigations ongoing
bullets: Police are investigating after a 9-year-old boy was allegedly filmed in a Jurong Point toilet cubicle.
The boy's father reported the incident after his son noticed a phone being inserted under the cubicle door.
The suspect reportedly left the scene before police arrived at the mall.
Mall management is cooperating with police investigations into the alleged voyeurism incident.

cards.headline: This Local Youth-Led Theatre Club Is Adapting George Bernard Shaw’s Pygmalion With A Singaporean Twist
bullets: A youth theatre club is staging a local version of George Bernard Shaw's Pygmalion in June 2026.
The play, 'Pygmalion: Mural of Singapore', is set in a Singaporean secondary school.
It follows a student preparing for a national debate competition and facing 'O' Level exams.
The production features cast and crew from various local educational institutions.
Tickets cost $30 and will be shown at the Drama Centre Black Box.
